benefits.title: Your EKG Is Clear. That 3 AM Racing Heart Has a Physical Trigger Your Doctor Is Missing.
benefits.description:
You bolt upright at 3 AM clutching your chest, gasping. Your pulse is racing, your throat is dry, your body is in full alarm.

Cardiologists clear you. You're told it's anxiety. You're offered antidepressants and sleep sedatives that leave you foggy and disconnected — and the 3 AM episodes keep coming.

Here is the physical trigger no one explained: declining estrogen during perimenopause structurally weakens your lower esophageal sphincter — the valve that keeps stomach acid where it belongs. When you lie flat, microscopic acid vapors leak upward and make direct contact with the vagus nerve running alongside your esophagus. Your brainstem reads this as an airway emergency and fires a survival-level adrenaline spike. That is what jolts you upright, heart hammering, every night.

SOMARA absorbs sublingually — directly into your bloodstream — and its concentrated botanicals coat the raw esophageal tract on the way down, providing a cooling herbal buffer that protects the vagus nerve from nocturnal acid contact. That is the difference between drugging your brain's alarm center and actually removing the trigger.

benefits.title: Yeast Creams Burn GSM Tissue. The Dryness Lives Deeper Than Any Cream Can Reach.
benefits.description:
The raw, dry, burning sensation between your legs is not an infection. It is Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause (GSM) — structural thinning of vulvovaginal tissues caused by estrogen withdrawal.

The lining that used to be plush, elastic, and self-lubricating is now paper-thin. Yeast creams and boric acid are formulated for fungal overgrowth, not tissue atrophy. Applied to already-compromised GSM tissue, they cause a searing chemical burn that makes the rawness significantly worse.

You have two tissue layers right now. The surface layer: topical creams occasionally soothe it briefly. The deep cellular layer: no cream you apply externally ever reaches the thinned pelvic floor from within.

Soursop (Graviola) and Irish Sea Moss in SOMARA work systemically — absorbed into the bloodstream, delivering rich cellular hydration directly to the thinned pelvic lining, restoring natural elasticity and moisture from the inside out. No burning. No application. No aggravating already-sensitive tissue.

benefits.title: Dark Clots Mean It's Working. The Older the Buildup, the Darker It Comes Out.
benefits.description:
Heavy. Dark. Almost black. Clots the size of a quarter.

Most women in perimenopause assume this means something is dangerously wrong and call their OB in a panic.

It is not infection. It is not a sign of disease. It is uterine stagnation — old endometrial buildup that accumulates when estrogen and progesterone fluctuate out of sync, preventing a complete, clean cycle month after month. The blood turns dark and thick because it has been sitting.

When SOMARA's botanical compounds begin clearing uterine stagnation — particularly the circulation-activating properties of Black Seed Oil, Ginger, and Turmeric — that accumulated buildup finally flushes. The darker and thicker the initial passage, the longer it has been sitting. Most women see the shift between weeks 2 and 4. As stagnation clears, cycles become lighter, less clotted, and more regular.

Every test comes back normal. Every specialist says you're 'just in perimenopause.' You're offered HRT, which helps somewhat — but your 3 AM heart episodes continue. The pelvic dryness persists. The clots keep coming.

HRT replaces the hormone signal. It does not repair the lower esophageal sphincter that has already structurally weakened. It does not reverse the mucosal thinning along the esophageal tract. It does not clear the endometrial buildup that has already stagnated.

Chlorella and Chlorophyll clear the cellular toxin accumulation that compounds with every sleepless night. Vitamin D3, B6, and C support tissue repair in the pelvic floor.

This is not a replacement for what you are doing. It is what addresses the physical damage that hormone balancing alone cannot reverse.
